QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_1

question.text: The SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 marked a significant transition in India's private capital industry. As a fund manager launching a new vehicle in 2026, which of the following BEST describes the industry-level transformation that the 2012 Regulations catalysed?

answer.text: A shift from a mutual fund industry to a portfolio management services industry with expanded retail access

The transformation of a predominantly Venture Capital and Private Equity industry into a full-fledged Alternative Investment Fund industry covering hedge funds, real estate, infrastructure and family offices
The migration of all offshore hedge funds to onshore status with SEBI now permitting leveraged retail hedge fund distribution
A regulatory convergence where AIFs, PMS and Mutual Funds were merged under a single licensing regime

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 states that post-2012 the industry evolved 'from a predominantly venture capital and private equity industry into a full-fledged alternative investment industry spanning several alternative asset management funds and UHNIs / family offices', explicitly including real estate, infrastructure and domestic/foreign hedge funds registered under AIF Regulations. The Trap: Option A conflates PMS with AIFs. Option C is wrong — offshore hedge funds were NOT auto-migrated; SEBI provided a limited FII window till 2012 and hedge funds got classified under Category III AIF going forward. Option D is fabricated — MF/PMS/AIF continue under separate regulations. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/XIX-B distributor exams emphasise the product landscape; XXI-B PM exam focuses on PMS evolution; XIX-C expects the Manager to articulate why the AIF Regulations 2012 is the inflection point for the entire alternatives industry. Manager's Pro-Tip: When pitching a debut fund to an anchor LP, frame your GP-track-record narrative around the 'post-2012 AIF era' — LPs bucket GPs by vintage cohort and pre-2012 VCF-era track record is given a different weight than post-2012 AIF track record.
